explanation: MFA typically uses factors in these categories: something you know (password), something you have (token, phone, hardware key), something you are (biometric), and somewhere you are (location). 'Something you have' is a recognized and commonly used MFA factor including hardware tokens, authenticator apps, and smart cards. The other options don't represent standard MFA factor categories.

why.A: Something you exhibit is not a standard MFA factor category; behavior-based authentication exists but isn't foundational.
why.C: Somewhere you are (geolocation) is not a primary MFA factor; it may be used for risk assessment but not core MFA.
why.D: Someone you know is a social engineering vector, not a security factor for MFA.

prompt: Easy-to-guess passwords led to an account compromise. The current password policy requires at least 12 alphanumeric characters, one uppercase character, one lowercase character, a password history of two passwords, a minimum password age of one day, and a maximum password age of 90 days.
Which of the following would reduce the risk of this incident from happening again? (Choose two.)

options.text: Increasing the minimum password length to 14 characters.
Upgrading the password hashing algorithm from MD5 to SHA-512.
Increasing the maximum password age to 120 days.
Reducing the minimum password length to ten characters.
Reducing the minimum password age to zero days.
Including a requirement for at least one special character.

answerText: Increasing the minimum password length to 14 characters.; Including a requirement for at least one special character.
explanation: Option A (increase minimum length to 14 characters) increases password complexity and entropy, making guessing harder. Option F (require special characters) adds a character class requirement that significantly increases the password space and prevents simple alphanumeric guessing. Together these address the root cause of easy-to-guess passwords. Options B, C, D, and E either don't address password guessing difficulty (B, C, E) or weaken it (D).

why.B: Hashing algorithm improvements don't prevent initial password guessing; they help only if the hash is already compromised.
why.C: Increasing maximum age to 120 days allows weaker passwords to remain in use longer, worsening the problem.
why.D: Reducing minimum length to 10 characters directly weakens password strength and increases guessing vulnerability.
why.E: Reducing minimum password age to zero allows immediate password changes, enabling rapid reuse and defeating history protections.

prompt: A user downloaded software from an online forum. After the user installed the software, the security team observed external network traffic connecting to the user's computer on an uncommon port.
Which of the following is the most likely explanation of this unauthorized connection?

options.text: The software had a hidden keylogger.
The user's computer had a fileless virus.

explanation: A backdoor is a hidden entry point installed by malware that allows attackers to remotely

access and control a compromised system. External network traffic connecting to the user's computer on an uncommon port after software installation is the classic indicator of a backdoor establishing command-and-control communication. Keyloggers don't establish incoming connections, ransomware focuses on encryption not remote access, and fileless viruses don't require traditional installation.

why.A: Keyloggers capture keyboard input but typically don't initiate external network connections to the infected machine.
why.B: Ransomware encrypts files and extorts users; it doesn't characteristically establish inbound remote access connections.
why.C: Fileless viruses run in memory without installation and don't match the download-then-connection pattern described.

prompt: A utility company is designing a new platform that will host all the virtual machines used by business applications. The requirements include:
•  A starting baseline of 50% memory utilization
•  Storage scalability
•  Single circuit failure resilience
Which of the following best meets all of these requirements?

options.text: Connecting dual PDUs to redundant power supplies
Transitioning the platform to an IaaS provider
Configuring network load balancing for multiple paths
Deploying multiple large NAS devices for each host

answerText: Transitioning the platform to an IaaS provider
explanation: Transitioning to an IaaS provider best meets all three requirements: IaaS providers maintain 50%+ baseline utilization through resource sharing across customers, offer built-in storage scalability through cloud infrastructure, and provide single circuit failure resilience through redundant data centers and multiple network paths by design. On-premises options like dual PDUs and NAS devices don't inherently achieve 50% baseline utilization or automatic geographic resilience.

why.A: Dual PDUs with redundant power supplies address power resilience but don't achieve baseline memory utilization targets or storage scalability requirements.
why.C: Network load balancing handles traffic distribution but doesn't address the 50% baseline memory utilization or storage scalability requirements.
why.D: Multiple NAS devices provide storage but don't achieve memory utilization baselines or single circuit failure resilience across the entire platform.

prompt: Which of the following best describes a use case for a DNS sinkhole?

options.text: Attackers can see a DNS sinkhole as a highly valuable resource to identify a company's domain structure.
A DNS sinkhole can be used to draw employees away from known-good websites to malicious ones owned by the attacker.
A DNS sinkhole can be used to capture traffic to known-malicious domains used by attackers.
A DNS sinkhole can be set up to attract potential attackers away from a company's network resources.

answerText: A DNS sinkhole can be used to capture traffic to
explanation: known-malicious domains used by attackers.

A DNS sinkhole is a security control that intercepts DNS requests for known-malicious domains and redirects them to a controlled IP address (often a local honeypot or monitoring server). This captures traffic destined for malicious domains, preventing users from reaching them and allowing security teams to monitor and analyze attack attempts. It's a defensive monitoring technique against known threats.

why.A: DNS sinkholes are security defensive tools; attackers don't view them as valuable resources for reconnaissance.
why.B: DNS sinkholes redirect away from malicious sites, not toward them; they protect employees rather than deceive them.
why.D: DNS sinkholes target known-malicious domains, not act as honeypots to attract attackers to company networks.

prompt: An incident analyst finds several image files on a hard disk. The image files may contain geolocation coordinates.
Which of the following best describes the type of information the analyst is trying to extract from the image files?
explanation: Geolocation coordinates embedded in image files are examples of metadata—data about data that describes properties of the files themselves. Metadata in images typically includes EXIF data, GPS coordinates, timestamps, camera information, and other embedded information separate from the image content itself.

why.A: Log data refers to system or application event records, not embedded information within files.
why.C: Encrypted data is scrambled content requiring decryption, not embedded geolocation information.
why.D: Sensitive data is a broad category; metadata is the specific technical term for this type of embedded file information.

prompt: Which of the following most likely describes why a security engineer would configure all outbound emails to use S/MIME digital signatures?
explanation: S/MIME digital signatures provide non-repudiation, meaning the sender cannot deny having sent the email because their private key created the signature. This cryptographic proof establishes authenticity and prevents senders from denying responsibility for messages they signed.

why.A: While compliance may be achieved through signatures, non-repudiation is the primary security purpose.
why.B: Digital signatures do not affect email delivery rates.
why.C: Signatures authenticate the sender but do not directly block phishing attacks; email filtering addresses that.

prompt: During a recent company safety stand-down, the cyber-awareness team gave a presentation on the importance of cyber hygiene. One topic the team covered was best practices for printing centers.
Which of the following describes an attack method that relates to printing centers?
explanation: Dumpster diving is a physical security attack where attackers retrieve discarded documents from printing centers and trash to obtain sensitive information. Printing centers are high-value targets because they handle large volumes of physical documents containing confidential data.

why.A: Whaling is a spear-phishing attack targeting executives, not specifically related to printing centers.
why.B: Credential harvesting involves collecting login credentials through digital means, not printing center operations.
why.C: Prepending is a technical attack involving adding false information to network packets, unrelated to printing.

prompt: Which of the following considerations is the most important regarding cryptography used in an IoT device?

options.text: The compatibility of the TLS version

explanation: Resource constraints—including limited processing power, memory, and battery capacity

—are the most critical consideration for cryptography in IoT devices. These constraints directly impact which cryptographic algorithms can be implemented, necessitating lightweight cryptography rather than computationally intensive solutions.

why.B: Bandwidth availability affects data transmission but is less fundamental than the device's ability to perform cryptographic operations.
why.C: Block cipher selection is important but derives from resource constraint considerations.
why.D: TLS version compatibility is relevant but secondary to whether the device can perform any cryptographic operations at all.

prompt: A coffee shop owner wants to restrict internet access to only paying customers by prompting them for a receipt number.
Which of the following is the best method to use given this requirement?
explanation: A captive portal is the best method for this scenario. It redirects unauthenticated users to a login/verification page where they can enter their receipt number before gaining internet access. This provides the necessary control over who accesses the network based on payment.

why.A: WPA3 is a wireless encryption standard that protects network traffic but doesn't restrict access based on receipt numbers.
why.C: PSK (Pre-Shared Key) requires all users to know the same password; it cannot differentiate between paying and non-paying customers.
why.D: IEEE 802.1X is an enterprise authentication framework requiring complex infrastructure; captive portal is simpler for this use case.

prompt: While performing digital forensics, which of the following is considered the most volatile and should have the contents collected first?
explanation: RAM is the most volatile form of storage and loses all data when power is removed. In digital forensics, volatile data collection must occur first because once the system is powered down or loses power, this evidence is permanently destroyed. Other storage types retain data longer.

why.A: Hard drives retain data even when powered off and are less volatile than RAM.
why.C: SSDs retain data after power loss, making them less volatile than RAM.
why.D: Temporary files, while volatile, reside on storage media that persists longer than RAM without power.

prompt: A hosting provider needs to prove that its security controls have been in place over the last six months and have sufficiently protected customer data.
Which of the following would provide the best proof that the hosting provider has met the requirements?
explanation: A SOC 2 Type 2 report provides audit evidence that security controls have been implemented and operating effectively over a specific period (typically six months or more). Type 2 specifically demonstrates control effectiveness over time, which directly proves that controls were in place and functioning to protect customer data.

why.A: NIST CSF is a framework for developing controls, not an attestation report proving their historical effectiveness.
why.C: CIS Top 20 compliance reports assess current compliance status but don't provide third-party attestation of control effectiveness over time.
why.D: Vulnerability reports identify weaknesses but don't prove historical control implementation and effectiveness.

prompt: A city municipality lost its primary data center when a tornado hit the facility.
Which of the following should the city staff use immediately after the disaster to handle essential public services?
explanation: The Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) is immediately activated after the disaster occurs to restore IT systems and critical data processing capabilities. DRP focuses on restoring technology and data, which is essential for a municipality to resume essential public services. BCP is broader and includes DRP as a component, but DRP is the specific tool for this scenario.

why.A: BCP (Business Continuity Plan) is broader and includes multiple components; DRP is the specific plan for this IT infrastructure failure.
why.B: Communication plan addresses stakeholder notification but doesn't directly restore technology services needed for public services.
why.D: IRP (Incident Response Plan) focuses on detecting and responding to security incidents, not restoring facilities destroyed by natural disasters.

prompt: Which of the following is considered a preventive control?
explanation: Segregation of duties is a preventive control that stops errors or fraud before they occur by ensuring no single person can complete a critical transaction alone. Configuration auditing, log correlation, and incident alerts are all detective controls that identify issues after they happen.

why.A: Configuration auditing detects unauthorized changes after they occur, making it detective.
why.B: Log correlation identifies suspicious patterns after events have been logged, making it detective.
why.C: Incident alerts notify of problems already occurring, making them reactive/detective controls.

prompt: A systems administrator notices that a testing system is down. While investigating, the systems administrator finds that the servers are online and accessible from any device on the server network. The administrator reviews the following information from the monitoring system:
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the outage?
explanation: The monitoring data shows that Test01 and Test02 are down despite being online and accessible from the server network. The key indicator is the dramatically high traffic received (654123168 and 651321685 bytes respectively) compared to traffic sent (14872 and 16941 bytes), showing an extremely asymmetrical traffic pattern. This characteristic imbalance of incoming traffic overwhelming outgoing traffic is typical of a Denial of Service (DoS) attack, where the systems are flooded with requests, consuming resources and making them unable to respond normally. The servers being accessible from other devices rules out physical jamming or routing issues.

why.B: ARP poisoning would redirect traffic but wouldn't create this specific pattern of massive incoming traffic with minimal outgoing responses.
why.C: Jamming is a physical layer attack affecting wireless signals and wouldn't allow the servers to remain accessible from the network as described.
why.D: Kerberoasting is a credential-based attack targeting Kerberos authentication and would not cause this type of traffic anomaly or general outage.

prompt: A security team has been alerted to a flood of incoming emails that have various subject lines and are addressed to multiple email inboxes. Each email contains a URL shortener link that is redirecting to a dead domain.
Which of the following is the best step for the security team to take?

options.text: Create a blocklist for all subject lines.
Send the dead domain to a DNS sinkhole.
Quarantine all emails received and notify all employees.
Block the URL shortener domain in the web proxy.

answerText: Block the URL shortener domain in the web proxy.
explanation: Blocking the URL shortener domain at the web proxy prevents access to the malicious links at the source, stopping the threat before users can click them. This is the most efficient and effective control that addresses the root vector of attack. Creating subject line blocklists is ineffective due to varied subject lines, DNS sinkholes don't address email delivery, and mass quarantine without targeting the specific threat vector is inefficient.

why.A: Subject lines vary in the attack, making blocklisting ineffective.
why.B: A DNS sinkhole doesn't prevent emails from being sent or accessed via web proxy.
why.C: Quarantining all emails is an overreaction and doesn't address the specific threat vector of the URL shortener.

prompt: A security administrator is working to secure company data on corporate laptops in case the laptops are stolen.
Which of the following solutions should the administrator consider?
explanation: Disk encryption directly protects data on stolen laptops by rendering the data unreadable without the encryption key, which is the primary concern stated in the scenario. Data loss prevention, OS hardening, and boot security address different security aspects but don't specifically protect data if a device is physically stolen.

why.B: Data loss prevention prevents unauthorized data exfiltration but doesn't protect data if the physical device is stolen.
why.C: OS hardening reduces attack surface but doesn't protect data if the device itself is stolen.
why.D: Boot security prevents unauthorized system access but doesn't encrypt data on the disk itself.

prompt: A company needs to keep the fewest records possible, meet compliance needs, and ensure destruction of records that are no longer needed.
Which of the following best describes the policy that meets these requirements?
explanation: A retention policy specifies how long records must be kept to meet compliance requirements and when they should be destroyed, directly addressing the need to keep the fewest records possible while meeting compliance and ensuring proper destruction. Security, classification, and access control policies serve different purposes in data management.

why.A: Security policy protects data but doesn't govern how long records are kept.
why.B: Classification policy categorizes data sensitivity but doesn't address retention duration.
why.D: Access control policy determines who can access data but doesn't specify retention periods.

prompt: Which of the following is a common source of unintentional corporate credential leakage in cloud environments?
explanation: Code repositories are a common unintentional source of credential leakage in cloud environments because developers frequently commit API keys, passwords, and tokens into source control systems, especially in public repositories. The dark web, threat feeds, and vulnerability databases are external sources, not sources of leakage, and state actors are not a source but rather threat actors.

why.B: Dark web is where leaked credentials are sold, not a source of organizational leakage.
why.C: Threat feeds provide intelligence about threats but are not sources of credential leakage.
why.D: State actors are threats that exploit credentials but do not serve as sources of leakage.
why.E: Vulnerability databases catalog known vulnerabilities but are not sources of credential leakage.

prompt: Which of the following is the best reason an organization should enforce a data classification policy to help protect its most sensitive information?

options.text: End users will be required to consider the classification of data that can be used in documents.
The policy will result in the creation of access levels for each level of classification.
The organization will have the ability to create security requirements based on classification levels.
Security analysts will be able to see the classification of data within a document before opening it.

answerText: The organization will have the ability to create
explanation: security requirements based on classification levels.

Data classification enables organizations to create differentiated security requirements and controls based on sensitivity levels, ensuring appropriate protection mechanisms for each classification tier. While end users benefit from awareness and access levels may be created, the fundamental purpose of classification policy is to establish risk-based security requirements that match the value and sensitivity of data.

why.A: User awareness of classification is a benefit but not the primary purpose of the policy.
why.B: Access levels are a result, but classification itself is about determining what controls are needed.
why.D: Security analysts' ability to see classifications is a tool benefit, not the primary purpose.

prompt: An analyst is performing a vulnerability scan against the web servers exposed to the internet without a system account.
Which of the following is most likely being performed?
explanation: A non-credentialed scan is performed without system account credentials, attempting to find vulnerabilities from an external, unprivileged perspective, which matches the scenario description. Packet capture captures network traffic, privilege escalation is a post-exploitation technique, system enumeration is part of scanning but not the name, and passive scans don't actively probe systems.

why.B: Packet capture collects network traffic data, not a vulnerability scanning method.
why.C: Privilege escalation is exploiting vulnerabilities after discovery, not the scanning method itself.
why.D: System enumeration is a component of scanning but not the specific scanning type being described.
why.E: Passive scans gather information without active probing, whereas this scan probes servers.

prompt: A security administrator is hardening corporate systems and applying appropriate mitigations by consulting a real-world knowledge base for adversary behavior.
Which of the following would be best for the administrator to reference?
explanation: MITRE ATT&CK is a real-world knowledge base documenting adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) based on threat intelligence, making it the ideal reference for hardening systems against actual adversary behaviors. CSIRT handles incident response, CVSS scores vulnerabilities, and SOAR automates incident response.

why.B: CSIRT is a team that responds to incidents, not a knowledge base for adversary behavior.
why.C: CVSS provides vulnerability severity scores, not adversary behavior information.
why.D: SOAR is a platform for automating security workflows, not a knowledge base for adversary tactics.

prompt: An architect has a request to increase the speed of data transfer using JSON requests externally. Currently, the organization uses SFTP to transfer data files.
Which of the following will most likely meet the requirements?
explanation: Microservices using APIs provide the modern, efficient way to transfer data using JSON requests over HTTPS. This directly addresses the requirement for faster data transfer using JSON externally while maintaining security. APIs are the standard approach for programmatic data exchange and are significantly faster than SFTP for high-volume transfers.

why.A: A website-hosted solution does not specifically enable JSON-based data transfer or improve speed over SFTP.
why.B: Cloud shared storage is not designed for fast JSON request-based transfers and doesn't address the speed requirement.
why.C: Secure email is unsuitable for data transfer and would be slower than current SFTP solution.

prompt: Which of the following addresses individual rights such as the right to be informed, the right of access, and the right to be forgotten?
explanation: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) specifically addresses individual rights including the right to be informed about data processing, the right of access to personal data, and the right to be forgotten (right to erasure). These are core principles of GDPR that do not appear as primary focuses in the other frameworks.

why.B: PCI DSS focuses on payment card security, not individual data rights.
why.C: NIST is a cybersecurity framework focused on risk management, not individual privacy rights.
why.D: ISO is a general standards organization; while ISO 27001 addresses data protection, GDPR specifically enshrines these individual rights.

prompt: An administrator is installing an LDAP browser tool in order to view objects in the corporate LDAP directory. Secure connections to the LDAP server are required.
When the browser connects to the server, certificate errors are being displayed, and then the connection is terminated.
Which of the following is the most likely solution?

options.text: The administrator should allow SAN certificates in the browser configuration.
The administrator needs to install the server certificate into the local truststore.
The administrator should request that the secure LDAP port be opened to the server.
The administrator needs to increase the TLS version on the organization's RA.

answerText: The administrator needs to install the server
explanation: certificate into the local truststore.

Certificate errors during secure LDAP connection indicate the server's certificate is not trusted by the client. Installing the server certificate into the local truststore will establish trust and allow the secure connection to complete successfully. This is the standard solution for certificate validation errors.

why.A: SANs are already supported in modern browsers and this wouldn't resolve certificate validation errors.
why.C: Port access for LDAPS is not the issue; the connection is being established but rejected due to certificate validation.
why.D: Increasing TLS version on the RA would not resolve trust issues with the server certificate itself.

prompt: Which of the following is the most important security concern when using legacy systems to provide production service?
explanation: Lack of vendor support is the most critical security concern for legacy systems. Without vendor support, security patches are unavailable, leaving the system vulnerable to known exploits indefinitely. This creates an ongoing and unmitigatable security exposure that organizations cannot address through their own efforts.

why.A: While instability is a concern, it affects availability rather than security directly.
why.C: Loss of availability is an operational concern but less critical than the ongoing security vulnerability from lack of patches.
why.D: Insecure protocols can be mitigated with network controls; lack of vendor support cannot be worked around.

prompt: A security investigation revealed that malicious software was installed on a server using a server administrator's credentials. During the investigation, the server administrator explained that Telnet was regularly used to log in.
Which of the following most likely occurred?

options.text: A spraying attack was used to determine which credentials to use.
A packet capture tool was used to steal the password.
A remote-access Trojan was used to install the malware.
A dictionary attack was used to log in as the server administrator.

answerText: A packet capture tool was used to steal the password.
explanation: Telnet transmits all traffic, including credentials, in cleartext over the network. A packet capture tool can easily intercept and extract the administrator's password from the network traffic. This is the classic vulnerability of Telnet and the most likely attack vector given the context of regular Telnet use.

why.A: Spraying attacks require knowledge of valid usernames and don't apply to a specific known administrator account.
why.C: A RAT would not be necessary when credentials can be easily captured from Telnet traffic.
why.D: Dictionary attacks require login attempts which would be detectable; passive packet capture is more stealthy and likely.

prompt: A user is requesting Telnet access to manage a remote development web server. Insecure protocols are not allowed for use within any environment.
Which of the following should be configured to allow remote access to this server?
explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) is the secure replacement for Telnet, providing encrypted remote command-line access to servers. It is the industry standard for secure terminal access and
is compliant with the requirement that insecure protocols not be used.

why.A: HTTPS is for web traffic, not terminal/shell access.
why.B: SNMPv3 is for network management, not server administration shell access.
why.D: RDP is for graphical desktop access, not typical for web server command-line management.
why.E: SMTP is for email, not remote server access.

prompt: A security administrator is working to find a cost-effective solution to implement certificates for a large number of domains and subdomains owned by the company.
Which of the following types of certificates should the administrator implement?
explanation: Wildcard certificates cover a domain and all its subdomains (e.g., *.example.com) with a single certificate purchase, making them the most cost-effective solution for protecting multiple subdomains. This single certificate can be deployed across numerous servers, significantly reducing costs compared to individual certificates per domain.

why.B: Client certificates are for authenticating users/devices, not for securing domains.
why.C: Self-signed certificates are not suitable for production external use and don't solve the multi-domain problem.
why.D: Code signing certificates are for signing code/executables, not for securing web domains.

prompt: An auditor discovered multiple insecure ports on some servers. Other servers were found to have legacy protocols enabled.
Which of the following tools did the auditor use to discover these issues?
explanation: Nessus is a comprehensive vulnerability scanner that identifies open ports and insecure protocols running on servers. It performs active scanning to detect security configuration issues, including enabled legacy protocols and exposed insecure ports, making it the appropriate tool for this type of audit.

why.B: curl is a command-line tool for transferring data, not for vulnerability scanning.
why.C: Wireshark is a packet analyzer for capturing and inspecting network traffic, not for port/protocol discovery.
why.D: netcat is a simple networking utility for connections, not a comprehensive vulnerability assessment tool.

prompt: A security analyst received a tip that sensitive proprietary information was leaked to the public. The analyst is reviewing the PCAP and notices traffic between an internal server and an external host that includes the following:
12:47:22.327233 PPPoE [ses 0x8122] IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 0, offset 0, flags [DF], proto IPv6 (41), length 331) 10.5.1.1 > 52.165.16.154: IP6 (hlim
E3, next-header TCP (6) paylcad length:
Which of the following was most likely used to exfiltrate the data?
explanation: The PCAP shows IPv6 traffic encapsulated within IPv4 (proto IPv6 (41)), which is IPv6-in-IPv4 tunneling. This encapsulation technique allows an attacker to hide IPv6 traffic within standard IPv4 packets to bypass security controls and exfiltrate data to an external host without detection. The unusual protocol combination and external destination indicate
deliberate use of encapsulation for data exfiltration.

why.B: MAC address spoofing would not be visible in the IP layer packet analysis shown and would not facilitate exfiltration to external hosts.
why.C: Steganography hides data within other media; there is no indication of hidden data within the payload itself.
why.D: The presence of encryption or lack thereof doesn't explain the exfiltration method; the data is being actively sent out.
why.E: Sniffing via on-path position captures traffic but doesn't explain how data was exfiltrated from the internal server.

prompt: A company wants to reduce the time and expense associated with code deployment.
Which of the following technologies should the company utilize?
explanation: Serverless architecture (such as AWS Lambda, Azure Functions) reduces deployment time and expense by eliminating the need to manage underlying infrastructure, provision servers, or handle scalability. The cloud provider manages all operational aspects, allowing developers to focus solely on code deployment and execution. This directly addresses the company's goal of reducing both time and cost.

why.B: Thin clients reduce client-side resource needs but don't address code deployment efficiency or expense.
why.C: Private cloud still requires infrastructure management and deployment processes, not reducing deployment time/expense as much as serverless.
why.D: Virtual machines require provisioning, configuration, and management overhead, still incurring deployment time and expense.

prompt: A security administrator is performing an audit on a stand-alone UNIX server, and the following message is immediately displayed: (Error 13):
/etc/shadow: Permission denied.
Which of the following best describes the type of tool that is being used?
explanation: The error message 'Permission denied' when attempting to access /etc/shadow indicates a password cracking tool is being used. Password crackers attempt to read the shadow file (which contains password hashes) to conduct offline attacks. The permission error occurs because the tool is running without sufficient privileges to access this restricted file. This is characteristic behavior of password cracking tools encountering permission barriers.

why.A: Pass-the-hash monitors would not generate permission errors when reading files; they monitor for pass-the-hash attacks.
why.B: File integrity monitors check file changes/hashes but wouldn't attempt to read shadow files or generate this specific error.
why.C: Forensic analysis tools typically run with elevated privileges and would not encounter basic permission errors on shadow files.

prompt: A security administrator needs to create firewall rules for the following protocols: RTP, SIP, H.323. and SRTP.
Which of the following does this rule set support?
explanation: RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol), SIP (Session Initiation Protocol), H.323, and SRTP (Secure Real-time Transport Protocol) are all protocols used for Voice over IP (VoIP) communication. SIP and H.323 handle call signaling and setup, while RTP and SRTP transport the actual voice data (encrypted in SRTP's case). These protocols are the
foundational technologies for VoIP systems.

why.A: RTOS (Real-Time Operating System) is not related to these communication protocols.
why.C: SoC (System-on-Chip) is a hardware architecture concept, not related to these protocols.
why.D: HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning) is a building management system unrelated to VoIP.

prompt: Which of the following best describes a social engineering attack that uses a targeted electronic messaging campaign aimed at a Chief Executive Officer?
explanation: Whaling is specifically defined as targeted social engineering attacks against high-level executives (C-level individuals like CEOs). It is a variant of phishing that uses tailored electronic messaging aimed at senior leadership. The term 'whale' refers to high-value targets. This matches the scenario of a targeted campaign against a Chief Executive Officer.

why.B: Spear phishing is targeted phishing but is not specifically defined for executive-level targets; it applies to any targeted individual.
why.C: Impersonation is a technique that could be used within whaling but doesn't describe the overall attack category.
why.D: Identity fraud involves assuming another's identity for personal gain, not sending targeted messaging campaigns to executives.

prompt: During a penetration test, a flaw in the internal PKI was exploited to gain domain administrator rights using specially crafted certificates.
Which of the following remediation tasks should be completed as part of the cleanup phase?
explanation: After exploiting a flaw in the internal PKI to gain domain administrator rights, the primary remediation task is patching the CA (Certificate Authority). This addresses the root vulnerability that was exploited and prevents future similar attacks. Patching the CA closes the specific flaw that allowed specially crafted certificates to elevate privileges.

why.A: Updating the CRL (Certificate Revocation List) would revoke certificates but doesn't fix the underlying PKI flaw.
why.C: While password changes are good practice, they don't address the PKI vulnerability that was exploited.
why.D: SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation and Response) is a tool platform, not a remediation task for PKI flaws.

prompt: A company wants to implement MFA.
Which of the following enables the additional factor while using a smart card?
explanation: When implementing MFA with a smart card as the first factor, a PIN (Personal Identification Number) serves as the second authentication factor. The smart card itself (something you have) is one factor, and the PIN (something you know) is the additional factor. Together they satisfy the MFA requirement of two different authentication types.

why.B: A hardware token is itself a physical factor similar to a smart card, not an additional factor to use with it.
why.C: User ID is typically username/identification, not an authentication factor—it identifies but doesn't authenticate.
why.D: SMS sends a one-time code but requires a phone; it's not the enabling factor specifically when using a smart card.

prompt: A company hired an external consultant to assist with required system upgrades to a critical business application. A systems administrator needs to secure the consultant's access without sharing passwords to critical systems.
Which of the following solutions should most likely be utilized?
explanation: PAM (Privileged Access Management) software is the ideal solution for granting secure temporary access to critical systems without sharing passwords. PAM provides credential management, session recording, access logging, and just-in-time privilege elevation. It allows the consultant to access systems through controlled sessions while maintaining security and audit trails, perfectly addressing the requirement to secure access without sharing credentials.

why.A: TACACS+ is an authentication protocol but doesn't provide the credential management and privileged access control needed.
why.B: SAML is a federation and SSO protocol for authentication, not specifically for managing privileged access without sharing passwords.
why.C: SSO provides unified authentication but doesn't address the secure delegation of privileged access to external consultants.
why.D: RBAC defines what users can do after authentication but doesn't solve the problem of securely granting temporary privileged access without password sharing.

prompt: A newly implemented wireless network is designed so that visitors can connect to the wireless network for business activities. The legal department is concerned that visitors might connect to the network and perform illicit activities.
Which of me following should the security team implement to address this concern?

options.text: Configure a RADIUS server to manage device authentication.
Use 802.1X on all devices connecting to wireless.
Add a guest captive portal requiring visitors to accept terms and conditions.
Allow for new devices to be connected via WPS.

answerText: Add a guest captive portal requiring visitors to accept
explanation: terms and conditions.

A captive portal with terms and conditions acceptance directly addresses the legal department's concern by creating a documented acknowledgment that visitors understand acceptable use policies and potential legal consequences for illicit activities. This provides both a deterrent and a legal record of user acknowledgment. While RADIUS, 802.1X, and WPS address authentication mechanisms, they do not specifically address the concern about visitors performing illicit activities or create the legal documentation needed.

why.A: RADIUS manages authentication but does not create accountability or legal acknowledgment for acceptable use.
why.B: 802.1X requires credentials but doesn't address the legal concern or create terms of service acknowledgment.
why.D: WPS weakens security rather than addressing concerns about illicit activities on the network.

prompt: Which of the following data roles is responsible for identifying risks and appropriate access to data?
explanation: The Data Owner is responsible for identifying risks associated with their data and determining appropriate access controls and permissions. This is a fundamental responsibility of data ownership. A custodian manages and maintains data, a steward ensures quality and proper use, and a controller determines how data is processed, but the owner specifically identifies risks and defines access policies.

why.B: Custodian manages and maintains data but does not determine access policies.
why.C: Steward ensures data quality and proper use but is not responsible for identifying risks and defining access.
why.D: Controller (in GDPR context) determines processing but is not the primary role for identifying access risks.

prompt: Which of the following physical controls can be used to both detect and deter? (Choose two.)
explanation: Lighting can both detect intruders through visibility and deter them by eliminating shadows and concealment. Sensors can both detect unauthorized access through triggering alarms and deter through visible notification. Fencing deters but primarily contains rather than detects; signage only deters; bollards only deter; locks only control access but do not detect.

why.B: Fencing primarily deters and contains but does not actively detect intrusions.
why.C: Signage only deters potential intruders; it does not detect anything.
why.E: Bollards deter vehicle access but do not detect unauthorized presence.
why.F: Locks control access but do not independently detect unauthorized attempts.

prompt: A multinational bank hosts several servers in its data center. These servers run a business-critical application used by customers to access their account information.
Which of the following should the bank use to ensure accessibility during peak usage times?
explanation: A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers, ensuring that no single server becomes overwhelmed during peak usage times, directly addressing accessibility during high demand. Cloud backups provide recovery but not real-time availability; geographic dispersal addresses disaster recovery but not peak load management; disk multipathing addresses storage redundancy, not web traffic distribution.

why.B: Cloud backups ensure data recovery but do not help handle peak usage traffic.
why.C: Geographic dispersal is for disaster recovery and redundancy, not peak load distribution.
why.D: Disk multipathing provides storage redundancy but does not address web server capacity during peak times.

prompt: The author of a software package is concerned about bad actors repackaging and inserting malware into the software. The software download is hosted on a website, and the author exclusively controls the website's contents.
Which of the following techniques would best ensure the software's integrity?
explanation: Code signing allows users to cryptographically verify that the software has not been modified and originates from the legitimate author. This prevents bad actors from repackaging malware-infected versions while maintaining the legitimate signature. Input validation protects against attacks but doesn't verify package integrity; secure cookies relate to web sessions; fuzzing tests for vulnerabilities but doesn't prevent tampering.

why.A: Input validation protects applications but does not verify the integrity of the downloaded package itself.
why.C: Secure cookies protect web session data but are irrelevant to software package integrity.
why.D: Fuzzing identifies vulnerabilities but does not prevent or detect malware injection into repackaged software.

prompt: A third-party vendor is moving a particular application to the end-of-life stage at the end of the current year.
Which of the following is the most critical risk if the company chooses to continue running the application?
explanation: The lack of security updates is the most critical risk when running end-of-life software. As vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited in the wild, the application becomes increasingly vulnerable without patches. While lack of support, features, and source code access are concerns, security vulnerabilities directly threaten system and data integrity, making this the most critical risk.

why.B: Lack of new features is a functionality issue but not a critical security risk.
why.C: Lack of support is problematic but less critical than unpatched security vulnerabilities.
why.D: Lack of source code access is rarely a primary concern for end-of-life applications.

prompt: A security analyst recently read a report about a flaw in several of the organization's printer models that causes credentials to be sent over the network in cleartext, regardless of the encryption settings.
Which of the following would be best to use to validate this finding?
explanation: Wireshark is a network packet analyzer that captures and displays network traffic at a detailed level, allowing verification that credentials are indeed being sent in cleartext over the network. This directly validates the reported vulnerability by inspecting the actual network packets. Netcat is a network utility but not designed for detailed packet inspection; Nessus is a vulnerability scanner but may not capture actual cleartext transmission; Nmap
performs port scanning and service discovery but doesn't analyze packet contents.

why.B: Netcat is a networking utility but not designed to inspect detailed packet contents for credential cleartext.
why.C: Nessus scans for vulnerabilities but doesn't directly capture and display cleartext credential transmission.
why.D: Nmap identifies open ports and services but does not analyze packet contents for cleartext data.

prompt: A development team is launching a new public-facing web product. The Chief Information Security Officer has asked that the product be protected from attackers who use malformed or invalid inputs to destabilize the system.
Which of the following practices should the development team implement?
explanation: Fuzzing (fuzz testing) deliberately feeds an application large volumes of malformed, unexpected, or random input to see whether it crashes, hangs, or behaves insecurely. That is precisely the threat described—attackers destabilizing the system with invalid inputs—so fuzzing is the practice that discovers and lets developers fix those weaknesses before release.

why.B: Continuous deployment is a release automation practice; it speeds delivery of code but does not test how the application handles malformed input.
why.C: Static code analysis inspects source code without executing it, so it cannot observe runtime instability caused by malformed input the way dynamic fuzzing can.
why.D: Manual peer review relies on human inspection of code and would not systematically exercise the application with thousands of invalid input combinations.

prompt: During an annual review of the system design, an engineer identified a few issues with the currently released design.
Which of the following should be performed next according to best practices?
explanation: When issues are identified in a system design during review, the appropriate next step is the change control process. This formal process ensures that identified issues are documented, evaluated, approved, and implemented in a controlled manner with proper authorization and documentation. While risk management and design review are related processes, change control is the specific mechanism for managing and implementing improvements to existing released designs.

why.A: Risk management would assess risks but doesn't directly implement solutions to identified design issues.
why.B: Product design process is for creating new designs, not for addressing issues in released systems.
why.C: Design review process identifies issues but doesn't implement changes; change control is needed to formally manage the corrections.

prompt: Which of the following is best to use when determining the severity of a vulnerability?
explanation: CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) is specifically designed to provide a standardized numerical rating of vulnerability severity, ranging from 0-10. It accounts for attack vector, complexity, privileges required, user interaction, and impact metrics. CVE is just an identifier, OSINT is intelligence gathering, and SOAR is for orchestration—none of these directly measure severity like CVSS does.

why.A: CVE is only an identifier/catalog number for vulnerabilities, not a severity rating system.
why.B: OSINT is open-source intelligence gathering, not a severity measurement tool.
why.C: SOAR is for security orchestration and automation, not for determining vulnerability severity.

prompt: An organization experienced a security breach that allowed an attacker to send fraudulent wire transfers from a hardened PC exclusively to the attacker's bank through remote connections. A security analyst is creating a timeline of events and has found a different PC on the network containing malware. Upon reviewing the command history, the analyst finds the following:
PS>.\mimikatz.exe "sekurlsa::pth /user:localadmin /domain:corp-domain.com /ntlm:B4B9B02E1F29A3CF193EAB28C8D617D3F327
Which of the following best describes how the attacker gained access to the hardened PC?

options.text: The attacker created fileless malware that was hosted by the banking platform.
The attacker performed a pass-the-hash attack using a shared support account.
The attacker utilized living-off-the-land binaries to evade endpoint detection and response software.
The attacker socially engineered the accountant into performing bad transfers.

answerText: The attacker performed a pass-the-hash attack using
explanation: a shared support account.

The command shown is mimikatz with the 'sekurlsa::pth' function, which executes a pass-the-hash attack. The attacker is using the NTLM hash of the 'localadmin' account (B4B9B02E...) to authenticate to the hardened PC without needing the plaintext password. This is a credential-based attack leveraging a compromised account hash from another system on the network.

why.A: Fileless malware and banking platform hosting are not indicated by the mimikatz command history shown.
why.C: Living-off-the-land binaries involve using legitimate system tools, but mimikatz is a dedicated hacking tool, not a LOLBin.
why.D: Social engineering of the accountant is not supported by the technical evidence of the mimikatz hash attack command.

prompt: Which of the following is the best resource to consult for information on the most common application exploitation methods?
explanation: OWASP (Open Web Application Security Project) is the authoritative resource for documenting the most common web application exploitation methods and vulnerabilities, particularly through publications like the OWASP Top 10. STIX is for threat intelligence sharing, OVAL is for vulnerability definitions, CVE is an identifier system, and threat feeds provide current intelligence but not the foundational methodology reference.

why.B: STIX is a data model for sharing threat intelligence, not a guide to exploitation methods.
why.C: OVAL is used for vulnerability assessment and detection, not documentation of exploitation methods.
why.D: Threat intelligence feeds provide current threat data but not comprehensive documentation of common exploitation techniques.
why.E: CVE is an identifier catalog, not an educational resource on exploitation methods.

prompt: A security analyst is reviewing the logs on an organization's DNS server and notices the following unusual snippet:
Which of the following attack techniques was most likely used?

options.text: Determining the organization's ISP-assigned address space
Attempting to achieve initial access to the DNS server

explanation: The log shows a DNS zone transfer (AXFR query) from an external IP (124.22.158.37) attempting to retrieve the complete zone file for int.comptia.org. The response reveals multiple internal DNS records (www, dns, adds, fshare, sip) with internal IP addresses (10.x.x.x range). This is a classic footprinting technique used to map an organization's internal network structure, DNS records, and IP addressing scheme. Zone transfers should be restricted to authorized secondary nameservers only, and this unrestricted transfer exposes internal network topology.

why.A: The log reveals internal private IP addresses (10.x.x.x), not ISP-assigned public address space.
why.B: DNS sinkholing is irrelevant here; this is about zone transfer enumeration, not malware detection or blocking.
why.D: There is no evidence of an attack against the DNS server itself; the attacker successfully completed the zone transfer, indicating no defensive measure stopped them.
why.E: While fshare data could theoretically be exfiltrated, the log shows only DNS reconnaissance/footprinting, not actual data exfiltration activity.

prompt: A security analyst at an organization observed several user logins from outside the organization's network. The analyst determined that these logins were not performed by individuals within the organization.
Which of the following recommendations would reduce the likelihood of future attacks? (Choose two.)

options.text: A review of user account permissions

answerText: Conditional access policies; Implementation of additional authentication factors
explanation: Conditional access policies (B) can restrict logins based on geographic location, device compliance, and risk factors, directly preventing unauthorized external logins. Implementation of additional authentication factors (D) such as MFA makes it significantly harder for attackers to gain access even with compromised credentials. Together, these provide both preventive controls (preventing unauthorized access) and detective controls (requiring stronger authentication).

why.A: Disciplinary actions don't prevent future attacks; these logins weren't from actual users within the organization.
why.C: More regular account audits detect issues after the fact but don't prevent unauthorized access from occurring.
why.E: Content filtering is irrelevant to preventing unauthorized user logins from external networks.
why.F: Reviewing permissions doesn't prevent attackers from logging in with compromised credentials in the first place.

prompt: A security team is addressing a risk associated with the attack surface of the organization's web application over port 443. Currently, no advanced network security capabilities are in place.
Which of the following would be best to set up? (Choose two.)
explanation: NIDS (A) provides network-level detection of malicious traffic on port 443, monitoring for attack patterns. WAF (E) is specifically designed to protect web applications by filtering and monitoring HTTP/HTTPS traffic for application-layer attacks. Both address the web application attack surface—NIDS provides network detection while WAF provides application-layer protection. These two complementary controls directly address the stated concern.

why.B: Honeypots are deceptive tools for threat research, not primary defenses for production attack surfaces.
why.C: Certificate revocation lists manage certificate validity, not application attack surface protection.
why.D: HIPS (host-based) protects individual endpoints but doesn't address network-level web application threats.
why.F: SIEM is for log aggregation and analysis, not a preventive control for web application attacks.

prompt: A systems administrator would like to create a point-in-time backup of a virtual machine.
Which of the following should the administrator use?
explanation: A snapshot is the appropriate tool for creating a point-in-time backup of a virtual machine. It captures the exact state of the VM at a specific moment, including disk, memory, and configuration, allowing administrators to revert to that state if needed. Replication is for redundancy, simulation is for testing, and containerization is for application packaging—
none provide point-in-time backup functionality.

why.A: Replication creates copies for disaster recovery but doesn't provide point-in-time restore capability.
why.B: Simulation is for testing scenarios, not creating backups.
why.D: Containerization packages applications, not VM backups.

prompt: A security administrator notices numerous unused, non-compliant desktops are connected to the network.
Which of the following actions would the administrator most likely recommend to the management team?
explanation: Decommissioning is the most appropriate action for unused, non-compliant desktops. These systems pose a security risk because they cannot be updated or maintained, making them vulnerable to exploits. Removing them from the network eliminates the attack surface they represent. While isolation, patching, and monitoring might temporarily mitigate risk, decommissioning permanently removes non-functional, liability-creating assets.

why.A: Monitoring doesn't solve the compliance issue or reduce the risk of non-compliant systems.
why.C: Patching unused systems that may not be updatable doesn't address fundamental non-compliance.
why.D: Isolating unused desktops leaves them on the network as potential liabilities; decommissioning is the proper lifecycle action.

prompt: Which of the following is a common data removal option for companies that want to wipe sensitive data from hard drives in a repeatable manner but allow the hard drives to be reused?
explanation: Sanitization is the process of securely removing sensitive data from storage media while maintaining the ability to reuse the hardware. It overwrites data in a repeatable manner using standards like DOD 5220.22-M, making recovery impossible while preserving drive functionality. This distinguishes it from degaussing (which destroys the drive) and simple formatting (which doesn't securely erase data).

why.B: Formatting does not securely erase data; deleted files can be recovered with forensic tools.
why.C: Degaussing destroys the hard drive with magnetic fields, making it unreusable for future purposes.
why.D: Defragmentation is a performance optimization technique unrelated to data removal.

prompt: An organization wants to improve the company's security authentication method for remote employees. Given the following requirements:
•  Must work across SaaS and internal network applications
•  Must be device manufacturer agnostic
•  Must have offline capabilities
Which of the following would be the most appropriate authentication method?
explanation: Time-based tokens (TOTP/HOTP) meet all requirements: they work across SaaS and internal applications, are device manufacturer agnostic (any TOTP-compatible authenticator works), and function offline without network connectivity. Username/password lacks multi-factor strength, biometrics require specific hardware, and SMS requires connectivity.

why.A: Username and password alone doesn't meet the multi-factor security requirement for remote access.
why.B: Biometrics require specific device hardware, violating the manufacturer-agnostic requirement.
why.C: SMS verification requires network connectivity and cannot work offline as required.

prompt: A security officer is implementing a security awareness program and has placed security-themed posters around the building and assigned online user training.
Which of the following will the security officer most likely implement?
explanation: A phishing campaign is a practical security awareness training tool that tests employee response to social engineering attacks. Combined with posters and online training, it demonstrates real-world threats and measures user compliance. The other options are security controls, not awareness program components.

why.A: Password policy is an administrative control, not part of awareness training implementation.
why.B: Access badges are physical security controls, not awareness program elements.
why.D: Risk assessment is an evaluation methodology, not an awareness program activity.

prompt: A malicious update was distributed to a common software platform and disabled services at many organizations.
Which of the following best describes this type of vulnerability?
explanation: A malicious update distributed through a legitimate software platform represents a supply chain attack, where the attacker compromises a trusted vendor to distribute malware to multiple organizations downstream. This affects the security of all organizations using that platform.

why.A: DDoS attacks target availability through traffic flooding, not software updates.
why.B: Rogue employees are individuals acting maliciously within an organization, not external supply chain compromises.
why.C: Insider threat requires a person within the target organization, whereas this originates from a software vendor.

prompt: A company web server is initiating outbound traffic to a low-reputation, public IP on non-standard pat. The web server is used to present an unauthenticated page to clients who upload images the company. An analyst notices a suspicious process running on the server hat was not created by the company development team.
Which of the following is the most likely explanation for his security incident?

options.text: A web shell has been deployed to the server through the page.
A vulnerability has been exploited to deploy a worm to the server.
Malicious insiders are using the server to mine cryptocurrency.
Attackers have deployed a rootkit Trojan to the server over an exposed RDP port.

answerText: A web shell has been deployed to the server through
explanation: the page.

A web shell deployed through the unauthenticated image upload functionality best explains the observed indicators: suspicious process, outbound traffic, and non-standard ports. Web shells are small scripts placed on web servers that provide attackers remote code execution and persistence. This attack vector specifically targets upload functionality.

why.B: A worm self-replicates across systems; the scenario describes compromise of a single server through targeted upload.
why.C: Cryptocurrency mining doesn't typically cause outbound connections to low- reputation IPs or match this attack pattern.
why.D: Rootkit Trojans require RDP access, but the attack vector described is the public-facing upload functionality.

prompt: An organization requests a third-party full-spectrum analysis of its supply chain.
Which of the following would the analysis team use to meet this requirement?
explanation: An illumination tool provides comprehensive supply chain analysis and visibility into vendor risk, dependencies, and potential vulnerabilities across the entire supply chain ecosystem. It maps relationships and identifies security risks throughout interconnected suppliers.

why.A: Vulnerability scanners identify technical weaknesses in systems but lack supply chain scope.
why.B: Penetration testing assesses security through active exploitation, not comprehensive supply chain analysis.
why.C: SCAP (Security Content Automation Protocol) is for vulnerability and compliance reporting, not supply chain analysis.

prompt: A systems administrator deployed a monitoring solution that does not require installation on the endpoints that the solution is monitoring.
Which of the following is described in this scenario?
explanation: An agentless solution performs monitoring without requiring software installation on
monitored endpoints. It typically uses API queries, SNMP, WMI, or other remote protocols to gather data, reducing deployment complexity and maintenance overhead.

why.B: Client-based solutions require installation on endpoints, contradicting the stated requirement.
why.C: Open ports refer to network accessibility, not monitoring architecture deployment models.
why.D: File-based solutions require local file access, implying agent or direct system interaction.

prompt: A security analyst is reviewing the source code of an application in order to identify misconfigurations and vulnerabilities.
Which of the following kinds of analysis best describes this review?
explanation: Static analysis examines application source code without executing it to identify vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and coding flaws. Code review is a primary static analysis method. This contrasts with dynamic analysis which requires runtime execution.

why.A: Dynamic analysis requires running the application to identify issues, not reviewing source code.
why.C: Gap analysis compares current state to desired state, unrelated to vulnerability identification in code.
why.D: Impact analysis assesses consequences of changes or incidents, not source code review for vulnerabilities.

prompt: Which of the following agreement types is used to limit external discussions?
explanation: An NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement) is specifically designed to limit external discussions and protect confidential information by legally restricting what parties can disclose about the relationship or information shared. BPA is a Blanket Purchase Agreement for procurement, SLA defines service levels, and MSA is a Master Service Agreement covering general terms—none of these are primarily used to restrict external discussions.

why.A: BPA is a procurement agreement, not designed to restrict discussions.
why.C: SLA defines service level commitments and metrics, not discussion limitations.
why.D: MSA covers general terms and conditions of service, not external discussion restrictions.

prompt: A security analyst is evaluating a SaaS application that the human resources department would like to implement. The analyst requests a SOC 2 report from the SaaS vendor.
Which of the following processes is the analyst most likely conducting?
explanation: Requesting a SOC 2 report from a vendor is a due diligence process where the organization evaluates the vendor's security controls and compliance posture before implementing their service. Due diligence is the systematic investigation and verification of a third party's security and operational capabilities. While attestation relates to the SOC 2 report itself, the process of requesting and reviewing it for decision-making is due diligence.

why.A: Internal audit evaluates the organization's own controls, not vendor evaluation.
why.B: Penetration testing is active exploitation testing, not vendor evaluation methodology.
why.C: Attestation is the auditor's assurance statement within the report itself, not the evaluation process.

prompt: Which of the following is used to conceal credit card information in a database log file?
explanation: Masking is the technique used to conceal sensitive data like credit card information in logs and other outputs by replacing characters with symbols or redacting portions of the data while maintaining the data structure. Tokenization replaces data with tokens for processing, hashing is one-way cryptographic transformation, and obfuscation is a general term for making data unclear—masking is the specific technique for concealing PII in logs.

why.A: Tokenization replaces sensitive data with tokens but is typically used in payment processing, not log concealment.
why.C: Hashing is a one-way function unsuitable for logs that need to display partial information.
why.D: Obfuscation is too general; masking is the specific, standard technique for this purpose.

prompt: A systems administrator is configuring a site-to-site VPN between two branch offices. Some of the settings have already been configured correctly. The systems administrator has been provided the following requirements as part of completing the configuration:
•  Most secure algorithms should be selected
•  All traffic should be encrypted over the VPN
•  A secret password will be used to authenticate the two VPN concentrators
INSTRUCTIONS
Click on the two VPN Concentrators to configure the appropriate settings.
summary: Configure the Phase 1 and Phase 2 settings on both VPN concentrators so the site-to-site tunnel comes up with the strongest available algorithms and encrypts all traffic between the branch offices.
steps: 1. Each concentrator must point at the other one's public address, so Concentrator 1 gets a peer IP of 5.5.5.20 and Concentrator 2 gets a peer IP of 5.5.5.10.
2. For the authentication method the answer key selects PKI on both devices, and the same method must be configured identically on each end or Phase 1 will fail.
3. Of the encryption choices offered, AES256 is the strongest (3DES is deprecated, BLOWFISH is weak, and ECC secp160r1 is not a symmetric cipher), so AES256 is chosen for both Phase 1 and Phase 2.
4. MD5 and SHA1 are both considered broken for integrity, leaving SHA256 as the most secure hash on every tab, and DH key group 14 is kept as the pre-set 2048-bit group.
5. Phase 2 must use ESP rather than AH because only ESP encrypts the payload; AH only authenticates it, which would not meet the requirement that all traffic be encrypted.

6. The local and remote network masks are entered as 255.255.255.0 to match the /24 networks (192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24) being carried through the tunnel, and the mirror-image values are configured on the other concentrator.

A site-to-site IPSec tunnel only forms when both ends agree on every parameter, so the two concentrators are configured as mirror images of one another: Concentrator 1 lists 5.5.5.20 as its peer and Concentrator 2 lists 5.5.5.10. The authentication method is set the same on both sides (PKI in the published answer). Where a choice of cryptography exists, the strongest option is picked - AES256 for encryption instead of 3DES or BLOWFISH, SHA256 for hashing instead of MD5 or SHA1 - and DH group 14 is retained for the key exchange. In Phase 2 the protocol must be ESP, since ESP provides confidentiality for the encapsulated packets whereas AH only provides integrity and authentication and would leave traffic in the clear. Finally the tunnel selectors are given the 255.255.255.0 mask so the full 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24 branch subnets are routed through and protected by the VPN, satisfying the requirement that all traffic be encrypted.

prompt: An organization recently started hosting a new service that customers access through a web portal. A security engineer needs to add to the existing security devices a new solution to protect this new service.
Which of the following is the engineer most likely to deploy?
explanation: A WAF (Web Application Firewall) is specifically designed to protect web applications and services accessed through a web portal by filtering and monitoring HTTP/HTTPS traffic for malicious requests. While firewalls and UTM devices exist, a WAF is the specialized solution for protecting web-based services. Layer 4 firewalls operate at the transport layer and NGFW are general network firewalls, neither specifically designed for application layer web protection.

why.A: Layer 4 firewalls operate at the transport layer and lack application-level web protection.
why.B: NGFW provides network-level protection but lacks the specialized web application filtering of a WAF.
why.D: UTM is a general security appliance; WAF is the specialized solution for web service protection.

prompt: Which of the following topics would most likely be included within an organization's SDLC?
explanation: Branch protection requirements are security controls implemented during the software

development process to ensure code integrity and governance, making them a direct component of SDLC. Service-level agreements relate to operational services, information security policy is organizational policy rather than SDLC-specific, and penetration testing methodology is a testing approach but not typically a core SDLC topic like branch protection which governs how code changes are managed.

why.A: SLAs define service performance expectations, not development lifecycle processes.
why.B: Information security policy is organizational governance, separate from SDLC specifics.
why.C: Penetration testing is a security testing methodology, not a core SDLC component.

prompt: Which of the following control types is AUP an example of?
explanation: AUP (Acceptable Use Policy) is a managerial/administrative control that establishes rules and expectations for how employees and users should behave with organizational resources. It is policy-based governance rather than a physical barrier, technical mechanism, or operational procedure. Managerial controls include policies, procedures, and administrative directives that manage risk through governance.

why.A: Physical controls are tangible barriers like locks or access cards, not policies.
why.C: Technical controls are technology-based like firewalls or encryption, not written policies.
why.D: Operational controls are day-to-day implementation procedures; AUP is a managerial policy.

prompt: An organization is adopting cloud services at a rapid pace and now has multiple SaaS applications in use. Each application has a separate log-in, so the security team wants to reduce the number of credentials each employee must maintain.
Which of the following is the first step the security team should take?
explanation: Selecting an IdP (Identity Provider) is the first foundational step before implementing single sign-on solutions like SAML or OAuth. The organization must choose which identity provider will manage user authentication before enabling any federation protocols or tokens. SAML and OAuth are protocols enabled after the IdP is selected, and password vaulting is a stopgap solution rather than the proper first step toward federation.

why.A: SAML cannot be enabled until an IdP is selected and configured.
why.B: OAuth tokens are created after IdP selection and configuration.
why.C: Password vaulting is a workaround, not the foundational first step toward proper SSO.

prompt: A company's online shopping website became unusable shortly after midnight on January 30, 2023.
When a security analyst reviewed the database server, the analyst noticed the following code used for backing up data:
Which of the following should the analyst do next?

options.text: Review WAF logs for evidence of command injection.
Scan the database server for malware.
Search the web server for ransomware notes.

explanation: The code shown is a SQL time bomb that executes a destructive command (DROP DATABASE) on a specific date and time (January 30, 2023 at midnight). This is a classic

example of insider threat sabotage planted by a database administrator. The website becoming unusable immediately after midnight on that exact date, combined with the discovery of this malicious code in the backup routine, strongly indicates intentional sabotage by a current or recently terminated DBA who had database access and knowledge to embed such code. Checking for recently terminated DBAs is the logical next step to identify the threat actor.

why.B: While command injection is a valid attack vector, this code is not injected from external sources but rather embedded in database procedures by someone with legitimate access.
why.C: Traditional malware scanning is not applicable here since the threat is legitimate code (SQL) with malicious intent, not a malware binary.
why.D: This is a database destruction attack, not a ransomware attack, so searching for ransomware notes on web servers is not the appropriate next step.

prompt: Which of the following would be the best way to test resiliency in the event of a primary power failure?
explanation: Production failover is the most effective way to test actual resiliency in the event of power failure because it involves an actual failure scenario with real systems under actual conditions. Parallel processing is an architecture approach, tabletop exercise is theoretical discussion, and simulation testing is less realistic than actual production failover testing. Production failover provides the most authentic test of whether systems will actually recover from a primary power failure.

why.A: Parallel processing is a system design approach, not a resiliency test method.
why.B: Tabletop exercises are theoretical discussions without actual system testing.
why.C: Simulation testing is less realistic than actual production failover testing.

prompt: Which of the following would be the most appropriate way to protect data in transit?
explanation: TLS 1.3 is a cryptographic protocol specifically designed to protect data in transit by encrypting communications between client and server. SHA-256 is a hash function for data integrity, not encryption. SSL 3.0 is outdated and deprecated due to security vulnerabilities. AES-256 is an encryption cipher but operates at the symmetric level and is not a complete protocol for protecting data in transit like TLS 1.3.

why.A: SHA-256 is a hashing algorithm for integrity verification, not for encrypting data in transit.
why.B: SSL 3.0 is deprecated and has known security vulnerabilities; TLS 1.3 is the modern standard.
why.D: AES-256 is a cipher but not a complete protocol; TLS 1.3 wraps encryption with authentication and key exchange.

prompt: Which of the following is a common, passive reconnaissance technique employed by penetration testers in the early phases of an engagement?
explanation: Open-source intelligence (OSINT) is a passive reconnaissance technique that gathers information from publicly available sources without direct interaction with target systems. Port scanning is active reconnaissance as it probes the target. Pivoting is a post-exploitation technique. Exploit validation involves testing exploits against identified vulnerabilities and is not passive reconnaissance.

why.B: Port scanning is active reconnaissance that directly probes target systems.
why.C: Pivoting is a lateral movement technique used after initial access, not reconnaissance.
why.D: Exploit validation requires active testing and interaction with the target system.

prompt: Which of the following threat actors is the most likely to seek financial gain through the use of ransomware attacks?
explanation: Organized crime groups are the primary threat actors seeking financial gain through ransomware attacks, as they operate profit-driven enterprises. Insider threats typically have different motivations (revenge, espionage). Nation-states pursue strategic and political objectives rather than direct financial gain. Hacktivists are ideologically motivated, not financially motivated.

why.B: Insider threats are motivated by revenge, ideology, or espionage rather than ransom payments.
why.C: Nation-states pursue strategic objectives and intelligence rather than financial ransoms.
why.D: Hacktivists are driven by ideological causes, not financial profit motives.
